root_idea.summary: The root expresses three principal orientations: inclination or bending, upward elevation and ascent, and a separate lexical branch referring to a quantified herd of camels.
root_idea.development: The meanings develop from bending and turning to limping, curved routes, and acts of inclining; the upward branch yields ascending movement and the stairs or ways by which ascent occurs. The camel-herd term remains a distinct inherited branch.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed as the adjective أَعْرَجُ, which is substantivized in the Quranic occurrences.
The Quranic plural مَعَارِجُ is displayed under its supported singular dictionary citation form مِعْرَاجٌ.

senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic imperfect forms describe upward movement toward a higher place or realm, including the movement of angels, the spirit, things, words, and affairs. The same upward-motion lexeme can also occur in a passive construction meaning to be taken upward.
In the Quranic occurrences the adjective is definite and substantivized, referring to the lame person or one characterized by lameness.

senses.definition: A stairway, ladder, or place or way of ascent.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural مَعَارِجُ. It denotes stairways in one occurrence and places or ways of ascent, including the route by which angels ascend, in another.
An alternative interpretation reported for the Quranic plural مَعَارِجُ in 70:3, distinct from the spatial sense of places or ways of ascent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To limp, walk with a limping gait, or become lame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited usages distinguish lameness caused by an accident from natural or chronic lameness according to the vocalization and construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The setting of the sun, or its inclination toward the place of setting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage associated with the verb describing the sun's movement toward setting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a male camel, to emit urine indirectly; a male camel characterized by this condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is specifically stated of the male camel when a hind girth presses upon the sheath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a building, structure, river, or rivulet incline.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form II usage describing the imparting of an inclination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn away from, leave, or forsake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs with عن in the sense of turning away from the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bend or incline toward someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction with على expresses turning or inclining toward an object; it also appears in idioms denying such inclination.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stay, pause, or remain intent upon something; to confine one's riding camel at a stopping place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction can describe remaining at a place or stopping for an object, including restraining a mount for one's travelling companions or a purpose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone lame.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give someone, or to possess, a herd of camels called عَرْج.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized herd-related usage distinct from the causative meaning ‘to render lame.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter upon the time of sunset.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized temporal usage of the Form IV verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become or be inclined, especially of a building or structure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form V usage describing an inclined form or position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pretend to be lame or imitate the gait of a lame person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VI usage involving imitation rather than actual lameness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bend or curve; of a road or travelers, to turn aside from a route.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb can describe a thing or road becoming curved, or a road or company of travelers declining from its course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive or exert oneself in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical form recorded as Lane R.Q. III.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large herd of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported size varies substantially among authorities, from roughly eighty or more to many hundreds or about a thousand; the plurals include أَعْرَاجٌ and عُرُوجٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Natural lameness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal designation of the condition of being naturally lame.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A river, rivulet, or valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is explained by the bending or inclining course of the watercourse or valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place or seat of lameness in the leg or foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical usage referring to the affected location rather than the general condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: High or elevated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival usage describing height or elevation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An affair not firmly, solidly, or soundly executed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival usage applied to an inadequately completed affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Midday, especially the intensely hot midday period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized temporal noun, commonly used with the definite article in the cited form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A traditional camel-watering schedule involving visits at specified morning, noon, or evening intervals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources report more than one detailed schedule under this term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The practice of eating only once each day.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized idiomatic usage illustrated by the expression that someone eats al-ʿurayjāʾ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Limping or slightly lame because of an accident.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited adjectival usage contrasts accidental lameness with a chronic ailment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for a crow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the crow's hopping or leaping gait.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for the female hyena; by extension, a plural designation for female hyenas.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited usage treats the feminine form as a specialized animal name and states that the male is not called أَعْرَجُ in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for a particular deaf, malignant serpent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal appellation distinct from the ordinary adjective ‘lame.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: Three nights at the beginning of the lunar month.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A calendrical usage recorded as a specialized plural term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular deaf and highly malignant serpent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The diminutive form denotes a specific serpent said to leap like a viper; its plural is الأُعَيْرِجَاتُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ladder-like thing or means by which souls ascend when taken from their bodies.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage, especially with the definite article, associated with the traditional account of the Miʿrāj; it is distinct from the Quranic general sense of places or ways of ascent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment or piece of cloth bearing curving stripes or lines.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal usage describing the pattern on the cloth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where a valley bends to the right and left.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun derived from the bending course of a valley.

cautions: The public headword مِعْرَاجٌ is the singular dictionary citation form; the Quranic occurrences in this group are the plural مَعَارِجُ.
The interpretation of مَعَارِجُ as ‘benefits or favours’ is an alternative Quranic interpretation reported for 70:3, not a replacement for its spatial ascent sense.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: Lane entry 2708, unit lane-unit:Erj:2708:g2:main, preserves a conflicting lexical reading: one tradition gives عَارِج as equivalent to غَائِبٌ, while another correction identifies the form as عَائِبٌ. The evidence is insufficient to assign either meaning confidently to this root.
